papers.title: Spatially resolved acoustic spectroscopy for selective laser melting
papers.abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) is a manufacturing technique that typically builds parts layer by layer, for example, in the case of selective laser melted (SLM) material by fusing layers of metal powder. This allows the construction of complex geometry parts, which, in some cases cannot be made by traditional manufacturing routes. Complex parts can be difficult to inspect for material conformity and defects which are limiting widespread adoption especially in high performance arenas. Spatially resolved acoustic spectroscopy (SRAS) is a technique for material characterisation based on robustly measuring the surface acoustic wave velocity. Here the SRAS technique is applied to prepare additively manufactured material to measure the material properties and identify defects. Results are presented tracking the increase in the measured velocity with the build power of the selective laser melting machine. Surface and subsurface defect measurements (to a depth of 24 m) are compared to electron microscopy and X-ray computed tomography. It has been found that pore size remains the same for 140 W to 190 W melting power (mean: 115-119 m optical and 134-137 m velocity) but the number of pores increase significantly (70-126 optical, 95-182 velocity) with lower melting power, reducing overall material density.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文不涉及生物医学植入物的多孔结构、应力屏蔽、疲劳测试或骨整合等主题，仅提供增材制造无损检测的背景知识。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not cover porous structure design, stress shielding, fatigue testing, or osseointegration for biomedical implants, nor does it involve LPBF fabrication of implant-specific materials.

summary_zh.motivation: 使用空间分辨声学光谱法无损检测SLM零件的缺陷和材料性能。
summary_zh.method: SRAS测量表面声波速度，与显微CT和电子显微镜对比验证。
summary_zh.result: 声速随制造功率增加而增加，低功率时孔隙数量显著增多。
summary_zh.validation: 光学显微镜和X射线断层扫描对比验证缺陷检测结果。

summary_en.motivation: To apply spatially resolved acoustic spectroscopy as a non-destructive evaluation technique for detecting defects and material properties in selective laser melted parts.
summary_en.method: The SRAS technique measures surface acoustic wave velocity, which is correlated with material density and defect content, and validated against electron microscopy and X-ray computed tomography.
summary_en.result: The measured velocity increases with build power, and the number of pores increases significantly at lower melting power while pore size remains constant.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed by comparing SRAS defect measurements with optical microscopy and X-ray computed tomography data.

papers.title: Compensation strategy to reduce geometry and mechanics mismatches in porous biomaterials built with Selective Laser Melting

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了选区激光熔化多孔生物材料的几何与力学补偿策略，直接关联刚度匹配和应力遮挡问题。
llm.why_not_core: Does not explicitly cover fatigue testing or osseointegration/surface morphology characterization.

summary_zh.motivation: 减少SLM多孔生物材料几何与力学性能偏差。
summary_zh.method: 提出补偿策略调整设计参数以匹配目标力学性能。
summary_zh.result: 有效降低了制造偏差，提高了刚度匹配性。
summary_zh.validation: 通过机械测试验证补偿后的力学性能。

summary_en.motivation: To mitigate geometric and mechanical mismatches in porous biomaterials fabricated by Selective Laser Melting.
summary_en.method: A compensation strategy was proposed to adjust design parameters for matching target mechanical properties.
summary_en.result: The strategy effectively reduced manufacturing deviations and improved stiffness matching.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical testing was conducted to validate the compensated mechanical performance.
